relevance_note: Case report of one GFAP-variant patient: "We report here an infantile case of AxD that is unusual both for its MRI features and for being heterozygous for a GFAP allele carrying a de novo p.Arg79His mutation".
method_note: Read by hand; output assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). Five in-scope people: the case-report patient (label 'patient'), her father (carries p.Glu223Gln) and mother (tested negative for p.Arg79His, normal GFAP allele; no variant row), and two previously published p.Glu223Gln carriers named in the Discussion with individual-level facts: 'ref (3) patient' (male, adult onset, hypertension/diabetes/alcoholism; diagnosis called equivocal by the authors) and 'ref (5) patient' (infantile, also carrying Y366H). Not given rows: the unspecified p.Glu223Gln-carrying parents of the ref (3) and ref (5) patients (only a group statement 'in each instance was also found in a parent', no individual detail); the other p.Arg79His cases of refs (4, 7) (group-level only); and the one heterozygous p.Glu223Gln carrier among 200 Italian healthy controls (a control subject mentioned only as a count, not described). Inheritance 'inherited unspecified parent' for p.Glu223Gln in ref (3) and ref (5) patients comes from the named-group statement 'three AxD cases (3, 5, this report), but in each instance was also found in a parent'. Y366H in the ref (5) patient is called 'de novo' but no parental testing is stated in this paper, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8); the gene for Y366H is not printed next to it and is taken from the paper's framing of AxD as caused by GFAP mutation. p.Glu223Gln pathogenicity and functional evidence come from sentences naming that exact variant and are applied to every carrier row; the cDNA c.667G>C for non-patient carriers comes from the paper's own pairing 'p.Glu223Gln (c.667G>C)'. Patient onset recorded as the age at presentation with seizures (9 months); delayed psychomotor development has no stated age. Age at last evaluation recorded as the age at death (17 years); the last dated examination was at 12 years and a repeat MRI 3 years after the first. Normal cranial circumference excludes abnormal head size but, under the narrow/broad rule, not the composite checklist item 'macrocephaly or megalencephaly' (left not reported). A normal ophthalmologic examination is recorded as the paper words it and excludes no specific eye-movement item. Normal metabolic tests recorded as excluded abnormalities of each named analyte. Parents: 'Both clinically unaffected parents' recorded as excluded 'signs of AxD'; no checklist item excluded from it. No contradictions found inside the paper. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say its patient was reported earlier.
